To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coupling between the isoscalar modes in a deformed system is very important, that it can be described in a self-consistent manner within the framework of the deformed QRPA, that the isoscalar response in a deformable system is very sensitive to the deformation, and that this sensitivity is very important for the determination of the nuclear in-compressibility from the experimental data.

the coupling between the isoscalar quadrupole and monopole modes is weak in deformed nuclei, and that it is not responsible for the discrepancies observed when extracting the incompressibility from experimental and theoretical monopole distributions.

(a) the coupling between the isoscalar giant quadrupole resonance and the isoscalar dipole giant resonance is not relevant in the determination of the nuclear in compressibility, (b) the coupling between isoscalar giant monopole resonance and the quadrupole resonance is important and should be taken into account when extracting the incompressibility from experimental data, (c) this coupling is stronger for the SkM$^*$ force than for the SLy4 force.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a detailed analysis of the isoscalar modes of excitation in deformed nuclei and their coupling with the deformation, in order to understand the role of the deformation in the extraction of the incompressibility from experimental data.
the study of the monopole and the quadrupole modes in deformed nuclei.

the study of the isoscalar giant resonances, and in particular the monopole mode in deformed nuclei, in order to understand the coupling between the isoscalar and the isovector modes and how it affects the extraction of the incompressibility.

the coupling of the two modes does not affect the extraction of $K_{\infty}$ from monopole distributions, at least for the nuclei considered here.
the isoscalar giant monopole resonance is a collective mode in deformed nuclei, which can be studied by means of the deformed Quasiparticle Random Phase Approximation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the coupling between the modes is not strong enough to affect the extraction of nuclear incompressibility, but that the deformed description is necessary to obtain a reliable estimate of the nuclear inelasticity.

the coupling between the monopole and the quadrupole modes, which we have studied by means of the so-called coupling strength $C$, can be neglected in a deformed nuclei, at least at low excitation energies.

the coupling between the monopole and the quadrupole modes is weak, and that the monopole response can be used to extract a nuclear incompressibility that is close to the value obtained for the spherical case.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coupling between the monopole and the quadrupole response can be strong enough to make the monopole response unphysical, and that this can be avoided if one uses a deformed description of the nucleus.

, when a coupling between the monopole and the quadrupole modes is present, the extraction of the incompressibility from a monopole distribution can be affected by a significant systematic error, that we quantify in the case of ${}^{24}{\rm Mg}$.
the quadrupole mode has a significant impact on the isoscalar response, especially for the monopole mode, which is strongly affected by the presence of the quadrupole coupling.
